analysis:
Examined all three excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Distributed/Onboarding/ClusterService.swift against the canonical index and supplied T-041 detail. The visible HEAD adds an optional child-environment input to the internal initializer (80–81, 165–173); the public initializer retains defaults (159–160). Storing this input alone establishes no authorization, encryption, data-exposure or billing regression. Existing surrounding logic uses a private service directory, exclusive service/command locks, paired-link responders, worker verification for model copies, and stop-before-restart supervision; these are context, not newly verified controls.
BASE 1124–1130 persists approvals set aside after local fallback; BASE 1295–1299 counts early member exits; BASE 1377–1404 selects coordinator-member versus local serving; BASE 1419–1438 launches and logs children. The complete range map identifies modifications to these interactions, but their HEAD implementations are outside the supplied excerpts: HEAD 1131–1133, 1301–1302, 1428–1429 and 1448–1463. The truncated patch does not establish their behavior, so no finding is supported here.
Integration must examine those HEAD lines and the new partEnvironment implementation/callers: whether child environment handling preserves DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and cache scope/storage controls (T-041), whether approval fallback preserves expiry/current authorization boundaries (T-052/T-053), and how changed quick-end accounting affects serving availability (A-018). Check whether environment overrides are test-only or reachable in production and whether secrets or security-sensitive settings are newly propagated or discarded. Missing source prevents a conclusion on these changed paths; the visible storage of an optional environment is not itself evidence of bypass.
